q: How many times longer is an onion skin cell than a yeast cell?
Which cells on the graph are simple cells? Use the graph to describe one difference from complex cells.
The bacterium. Simple cells are much smaller: 2 micrometres compared with 6 to 200 for complex cells (they also have no nucleus).
1000 micrometres = 1 mm. A student says she saw a single bacterium clearly with a hand lens that magnifies x10. Evaluate this claim.

A bacterium is 2 micrometres = 0.002 mm. At x10 it would look 0.02 mm long, far below what the eye can see (about 0.1 mm). So she cannot have seen one bacterium; she may have seen a colony of millions.
